subject: math
title: Addition and Subtraction Strategies
seo_title: Grade 1 Addition and Subtraction Strategies Worksheets: Turn-Around Facts, Counting On and Fact Families
standard_text: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.) To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 addition and subtraction strategies worksheets: turn-around facts, make a ten, count on and count back on a number line, fact families, and subtract by thinking addition. 100 1st grade practice questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: If you know 8 + 3 = 11, you also know 3 + 8 = 11, 11 − 3 = 8 and 11 − 8 = 3.
key_sub: Count on from the bigger number: 9 + 3 is 10, 11, 12. Make a ten: 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. To find 13 − 9, think 9 + ? = 13.
body_html:
Use what you know

You do not have to count every fact from 1. If you know one fact, you know more facts. These strategies help you add and subtract fast.

Turn-around facts

Change the order. The sum stays the same.

With three numbers, add the two that make 10 first.

Make a ten

2 + 6 + 4 = ?

Look for two numbers that make 10: 6 + 4 = 10. Then 2 + 10 = 12.

Answer: 12

Count on and count back

To add a small number, start at the bigger number and count on. To take away a small number, count back. Do not count the number you start on.

Count back

12 − 2 = ?

Start at 12. Count back 2: 11, 10.

Answer: 10

Fact families

3 numbers can make 4 facts. They all use the same 3 numbers.

Subtract: think addition

To find 13 − 9, ask: 9 + what = 13? Count up from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 4.

Example

10 − 8 = ?

Think: 8 + ? = 10. 8 + 2 = 10.

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
9 + 3: “9, 10, 11”, so 11Do not count 9. Say the next 3 numbers: 10, 11, 12
12 − 2: “12, 11”, so 11Start at 12 and count back 2: 11, 10. So 10
Counting on from the small number: 2 + 9Start at 9 and count on 2: 10, 11
8 − 3 = 5 in the family of 3, 8 and 11A family uses only its 3 numbers. 5 is not one of them
13 − 9: “9 − 3 = 6”, so 16Think addition: 9 + 4 = 13, so 13 − 9 = 4

faq.q: What are addition and subtraction strategies in 1st grade?
faq.a: First graders use turn-around facts (8 + 3 = 3 + 8), making a ten, counting on and counting back, fact families, and thinking addition to subtract. These come from Common Core standards 1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.B.4 and 1.OA.C.5.
A turn-around fact has the same two numbers in a different order, like 8 + 3 and 3 + 8. The sum is the same, so knowing one fact gives you the other one free.

faq.q: How do you teach counting on in Grade 1?
faq.a: Start at the bigger number and say the next numbers, one for each number you add. For 9 + 3, say “10, 11, 12”. Do not count the 9 again.

faq.q: How does addition help with subtraction?
faq.a: Subtraction is finding a missing part. To solve 13 − 9, ask “9 plus what makes 13?” Since 9 + 4 = 13, the answer is 4.

sets.title: Turn-around facts and make a ten

items.q: 5 + 2 = 7. The domino turns around. What is 2 + 5?
items.e: The domino has the same dots: 2 and 5. 2 + 5 = 5 + 2 = 7. Turn-around facts have the same sum.

items.q: 4 + 6 = 10. The domino turns around. What is 6 + 4?
items.e: The domino has the same dots: 6 and 4. 6 + 4 = 4 + 6 = 10. Turn-around facts have the same sum.

items.q: 6 + 3 = 9. The domino turns around. What is 3 + 6?
items.e: The domino has the same dots: 3 and 6. 3 + 6 = 6 + 3 = 9. Turn-around facts have the same sum.

items.q: 1 + 5 = 6. The domino turns around. What is 5 + 1?
items.e: The domino has the same dots: 5 and 1. 5 + 1 = 1 + 5 = 6. Turn-around facts have the same sum.

items.q: The top train shows 8 + 3 = 11. The bottom train is the same train turned around. What fact does it show?
items.e: The bottom train has the same cubes: 3 green and 8 red. 3 + 8 = 11. Changing the order does not change the sum.

items.q: The top train shows 9 + 4 = 13. The bottom train is the same train turned around. What fact does it show?
items.e: The bottom train has the same cubes: 4 green and 9 red. 4 + 9 = 13. Changing the order does not change the sum.

items.q: The top train shows 7 + 5 = 12. The bottom train is the same train turned around. What fact does it show?
items.e: The bottom train has the same cubes: 5 green and 7 red. 5 + 7 = 12. Changing the order does not change the sum.

items.q: The top train shows 6 + 9 = 15. The bottom train is the same train turned around. What fact does it show?
items.e: The bottom train has the same cubes: 9 green and 6 red. 9 + 6 = 15. Changing the order does not change the sum.
Both sides use the same two numbers, 6 and 9. So the missing number is 6. Both sides are 15.
Both sides use the same two numbers, 5 and 7. So the missing number is 5. Both sides are 12.
Both sides use the same two numbers, 4 and 8. So the missing number is 8. Both sides are 12.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 + 9?
items.e: Switch the order: 4 + 9 = 9 + 4 = 13. 9 − 4 is 5, not 13.

items.q: You know 7 + 2 = 9. Which fact do you also know?
items.e: Turn it around: 2 + 7 = 9 too. The sum stays the same.

items.q: You know 10 + 6 = 16. Which fact do you also know?
items.e: Turn it around: 6 + 10 = 16 too. The sum stays the same.

items.q: Luis wants to count on to find 2 + 9. What is the fastest way?
items.e: 2 + 9 = 9 + 2. Start at the bigger number. Then there are only 2 numbers to say: 10, 11. 2 + 9 = 11.

items.q: Eli wants to count on to find 3 + 8. What is the fastest way?
items.e: 3 + 8 = 8 + 3. Start at the bigger number. Then there are only 3 numbers to say: 9, 10, 11. 3 + 8 = 11.
Add the two numbers that make 10 first: 7 + 3 = 10. The 5 is left. So the missing number is 5.
Add the two numbers that make 10 first: 6 + 4 = 10. The 2 is left. So the missing number is 2.

items.q: Which fact does the number line show?
items.e: Start at 7. There are 4 jumps to the right. Right means add. 7 + 4 = 11.

items.q: Which fact does the number line show?
items.e: Start at 11. There are 3 jumps to the right. Right means add. 11 + 3 = 14.

items.q: Which fact does the number line show?
items.e: Start at 14. There are 4 jumps to the left. Left means subtract. 14 − 4 = 10.

items.q: Which fact does the number line show?
items.e: Start at 10. There are 2 jumps to the left. Left means subtract. 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: Kai counts on to find 8 + 3. What does he say?
items.e: Start at 8 and say the next 3 numbers: 9, 10, 11. So 8 + 3 = 11.

items.q: Emma counts on to find 5 + 4. What does she say?
items.e: Start at 5 and say the next 4 numbers: 6, 7, 8, 9. So 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: Ben counts back to find 14 − 3. What does he say?
items.e: Start at 14 and count back 3: 13, 12, 11. So 14 − 3 = 11.

items.q: Count on. 2 + 7 = ?
items.e: Start at the bigger number, 7. Count on 2: 8, 9. 2 + 7 = 9.

items.q: Count on. 3 + 9 = ?
items.e: Start at the bigger number, 9. Count on 3: 10, 11, 12. 3 + 9 = 12.

items.q: Count back. 17 − 3 = ?
items.e: Start at 17. Count back 3: 16, 15, 14. 17 − 3 = 14.

items.q: Count back. 11 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 11. Count back 2: 10, 9. 11 − 2 = 9.

items.q: Which fact is in this fact family?
items.e: This family uses only 3, 8 and 11. 11 − 3 = 8 uses only these numbers. The other facts are true, but they use a different number.

items.q: Which fact is in this fact family?
items.e: This family uses only 4, 9 and 13. 9 + 4 = 13 uses only these numbers. The other facts are true, but they use a different number.

items.q: Which fact is in this fact family?
items.e: This family uses only 5, 7 and 12. 12 − 7 = 5 uses only these numbers. The other facts are true, but they use a different number.

items.q: Which fact is in this fact family?
items.e: This family uses only 6, 8 and 14. 14 − 8 = 6 uses only these numbers. The other facts are true, but they use a different number.

items.q: Which fact is in this fact family?
items.e: This family uses only 2, 9 and 11. 11 − 9 = 2 uses only these numbers. The other facts are true, but they use a different number.

items.q: Which fact is in this fact family?
items.e: This family uses only 7, 9 and 16. 16 − 7 = 9 uses only these numbers. The other facts are true, but they use a different number.

items.q: Which three numbers make a fact family?
items.e: 5 + 7 = 12, so 5, 7, 12 make a family. Check the others: 5 + 7 is not 13, 5 + 6 is not 12, 4 + 7 is not 12.

items.q: Two numbers must add up to the third. Which three numbers make a fact family?
items.e: 4 + 8 = 12, so 4, 8, 12 make a family. Check the others: 4 + 8 is not 13, 4 + 7 is not 12, 3 + 8 is not 12.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family of 2, 7 and 9?
items.e: 7 − 2 = 5 uses 5, which is not in the family. The family of 2, 7 and 9: 2 + 7 = 9, 7 + 2 = 9, 9 − 2 = 7, 9 − 7 = 2.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family of 5, 6 and 11?
items.e: 6 − 5 = 1 uses 1, which is not in the family. The family of 5, 6 and 11: 5 + 6 = 11, 6 + 5 = 11, 11 − 5 = 6, 11 − 6 = 5.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family of 3, 9 and 12?
items.e: 9 + 4 = 13 uses 4 and 13, which are not in the family. The family of 3, 9 and 12: 3 + 9 = 12, 9 + 3 = 12, 12 − 3 = 9, 12 − 9 = 3.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family of 7, 8 and 15?
items.e: 15 − 6 = 9 uses 6 and 9, which are not in the family. The family of 7, 8 and 15: 7 + 8 = 15, 8 + 7 = 15, 15 − 7 = 8, 15 − 8 = 7.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family of 4, 6 and 10?
items.e: 6 − 4 = 2 uses 2, which is not in the family. The family of 4, 6 and 10: 4 + 6 = 10, 6 + 4 = 10, 10 − 4 = 6, 10 − 6 = 4.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family of 8, 9 and 17?
items.e: 17 + 8 = 25 uses 25, which is not in the family. The family of 8, 9 and 17: 8 + 9 = 17, 9 + 8 = 17, 17 − 8 = 9, 17 − 9 = 8.

items.q: You know 9 + 6 = 15. Which subtraction fact do you also know?
items.e: Start with the biggest number, 15. Take away 6, and 9 is left: 15 − 6 = 9. You cannot take 15 away from 6.

items.q: You know 8 + 4 = 12. Which subtraction fact do you also know?
items.e: Start with the biggest number, 12. Take away 4, and 8 is left: 12 − 4 = 8. You cannot take 12 away from 4.
The last fact is 13 − 6 = 7. Check: 6 + 7 = 13.
The last fact is 14 − 5 = 9. Check: 5 + 9 = 14.

items.q:
13 − 9 = ?
Think: 9 + ? = 13
items.e: The whole is 13. One part is 9. Count up from 9 to 13: 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 4. 9 + 4 = 13, so 13 − 9 = 4.

items.q:
11 − 8 = ?
Think: 8 + ? = 11
items.e: The whole is 11. One part is 8. Count up from 8 to 11: 9, 10, 11. That is 3. 8 + 3 = 11, so 11 − 8 = 3.

items.e: The whole is 15. One part is 7. Count up from 7 to 15: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 8. 7 + 8 = 15, so 15 − 7 = 8.

Think: 6 + ? = 14
items.e: The whole is 14. One part is 6. Count up from 6 to 14: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. That is 8. 6 + 8 = 14, so 14 − 6 = 8.

items.q: Which addition fact helps you find 15 − 7?
items.e: Think: 7 + what = 15? 7 + 8 = 15, so 15 − 7 = 8. 15 + 7 = 22 is true, but it does not help.

items.q: Which addition fact helps you find 13 − 8?
items.e: Think: 8 + what = 13? 8 + 5 = 13, so 13 − 8 = 5. 13 + 8 = 21 is true, but it does not help.

items.q: Which addition fact helps you find 11 − 6?
items.e: Think: 6 + what = 11? 6 + 5 = 11, so 11 − 6 = 5. 11 + 6 = 17 is true, but it does not help.

items.q: Which addition fact helps you find 16 − 9?
items.e: Think: 9 + what = 16? 9 + 7 = 16, so 16 − 9 = 7. 16 + 9 = 25 is true, but it does not help.
Think addition: 6 + 8 = 14. Check: 14 − 6 = 8.
Think addition: 9 + 3 = 12. Check: 12 − 9 = 3.
Think addition: 4 + 7 = 11. Check: 11 − 4 = 7.

items.q: Which fact is true?
items.e: Check with addition: 9 + 7 = 16, so 16 − 9 = 7 is right. Do not do 9 − 6 = 3 and write 13.

items.q: Check with addition. Which fact is right?
items.e: Check with addition: 8 + 6 = 14, so 14 − 8 = 6 is right. Do not do 8 − 4 = 4 and write 14.

items.q: Which one is correct?
items.e: Check with addition: 5 + 7 = 12, so 12 − 5 = 7 is right. Do not do 5 − 2 = 3 and write 13.

items.q: Sam has 3 red cars and 9 blue cars. How many cars does he have?
items.e: Put them together: 3 + 9 = 9 + 3. Start at 9 and count on 3: 10, 11, 12. That is 12 cars.

items.q: Grace has 2 apples. She gets 8 more. How many apples does she have now?
items.e: 2 + 8 = 8 + 2. Start at 8 and count on 2: 9, 10. That is 10 apples.

items.q: There are 12 birds in a tree. 2 birds fly away. How many birds are left?
items.e: Some fly away, so subtract. Start at 12 and count back 2: 11, 10. That is 10 birds.

items.q: There are 16 kids in a class. 3 kids go to the library. How many kids are still in the class?
items.e: Some go away, so subtract. Start at 16 and count back 3: 15, 14, 13. That is 13 kids.

items.q: Mia read 6 pages on Monday. She read 4 pages on Tuesday. How many pages did she read in all?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10 pages. Start at 6 and count on 4: 7, 8, 9, 10.

items.q: Lily has 10 grapes. She eats 8. How many grapes are left?
items.e: 10 − 8 = ? Think: 8 + 2 = 10. So 2 grapes are left.

items.q: There are 11 kids at the park. 9 kids go home. How many kids are still at the park?
items.e: 11 − 9 = ? Think: 9 + 2 = 11. So 2 kids are still there.

items.q: Jack has 13 stickers. He gives 9 to Nora. How many stickers does Jack have left?
items.e: 13 − 9 = ? Think: 9 + 4 = 13. So Jack has 4 stickers left.

items.q: Zoe has 7 shells. She wants 15 shells. How many more shells does she need?
items.e: Think: 7 + ? = 15. 7 + 3 = 10, and 5 more is 15. 3 + 5 = 8. Zoe needs 8 more shells.

items.q: A tank has 6 fish. The class puts in 9 more fish. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: 6 + 9 = 9 + 6. Start at 9. 9 + 1 = 10, and 5 more is 15. That is 15 fish.

items.q: Omar has 2 cookies. He gets 9 more. What is the fastest way to find how many he has?
items.e: 2 + 9 = 9 + 2. Start at the bigger number, 9, and count on 2: 10, 11. Omar has 11 cookies.

items.q: Owen has 4 red marbles, 7 blue marbles and 6 green marbles. How many marbles does he have in all?
items.e: Make a ten first: 4 + 6 = 10. Then 10 + 7 = 17 marbles.

items.q: A pet shop has 5 cats, 3 dogs and 5 rabbits. How many pets is that?
items.e: Make a ten first: 5 + 5 = 10. Then 10 + 3 = 13 pets.

items.q: Maya has 4 red beads and 7 blue beads. Luis has 7 red beads and 4 blue beads. Who has more beads?
items.e: 4 + 7 = 11 and 7 + 4 = 11. Turn-around facts have the same sum, so they have the same number of beads.

items.q: Eli makes a cube train with 6 red cubes and 8 blue cubes. Kai uses 8 red cubes and 6 blue cubes. Who uses more cubes?
items.e: 6 + 8 = 14 and 8 + 6 = 14. Both trains have 14 cubes.

items.q: There are 12 birds. Some fly away. Now 8 birds are left. Which fact helps you find how many flew away?
items.e: 8 birds are left. 8 and the birds that flew away make 12: 8 + 4 = 12. So 4 birds flew away.

items.q: Emma has 9 blocks. She needs 16 blocks. Which fact finds how many more blocks she needs?
items.e: Emma has 9 and needs 16. 9 + 7 = 16, so she needs 7 more blocks.

items.q: Ben has 15 crayons. He loses some. Now he has 9. Which fact finds how many he lost?
items.e: 15 take away some is 9. Think: 9 + 6 = 15. So 15 − 6 = 9, and he lost 6 crayons.

items.q: Some ducks are in a pond. 5 more ducks come. Now there are 13 ducks. How many ducks were there at first?
items.e: Think: ? + 5 = 13. 8 + 5 = 13, so there were 8 ducks at first. Check: 13 − 5 = 8.

items.q: Grace knows 8 + 5 = 13. She has 13 plums. She gives 5 to friends. How many plums are left?
items.e: 13 − 5 is in the same family as 8 + 5 = 13. So 13 − 5 = 8. 8 plums are left.
